Duffett, Allum, Rice and Khlopin (who is not allowed to compete owing to his Russian nationality) travelled to Beaconsfield to run in the National Championship.

It was to have been a 3 aside match, but only 2 L A.C. men turned out, Ries and Sargant, the Bels, being Rice, Duffett and Webb. Ries went away in the lead, followed by Duffett and Rice, with the other L.A.C. man in the rear.
On the same day Fred Port won the 100yds Handicap at the Southgate and Wood Green meeting and our team (Penny, Footer and Rice) won the three miles Team Handicap Race.

Bill Rice finished for us an easy winner, thus retaining our unbeaten record of some years standing in this event. The Mile Team Race, which we have always won in recent years, gave us another victory Bill Webb was first man home, followed by Norman Gunn, of Mitcham A.C.
Rice was placed third in the Mile Championship and both Duffett and Footer gained standard medals. Rice's time (approximately 4min. 31secs.) is the best he has yet achieved.
The Club's thanks and congratulations are due to Messrs. Webb, Penny, Rice and Flower (T. J.) for the part they played in retaining the "Jockey" Cup for the Club sideboard.

This year there seems to have sprung up a new method of running miles; that is by running two comparatively slow quarters—of equal times—for the first half, followed by two fast ones, and our championship was run in this fashion. At the quarter Rice had what the journalists call a nominal lead from T.
Sixteen men lined up at the start, and it was thought before hand that it would be a race between Penny, Rice and Kench, but I believe the last-named was really the favourite.

Mains was on Carter's shoulder, then came our "second Footer"—Harry Shields—nearly a minute behind Penny! Cook, Rice, Shaw and Walker were in a string after this. Mention should be made of Shaw, who was in very experienced company.

Our other men were at this time not doing too well, for Rice and Walker were in the 30's. They were, however, closely followed by Robertshaw, Mitchell and Cecil Penny.

Webb 62, Rice 74, Allum 102. In 1930 the race was staged from Brighton Racecourse Stand, over a difficult course, with its ascents and descents of the Sussex Downs; but the finish found us jubilant at gaining third place for the first time, and optimistic about future years.

In a fast start Chantler was the best away, but was soon headed by Syd Warboys moving in his best style and taking the field along at a fast pace for about ¾ mile, when Tom Carter moved up to take the lead, followed closely by Allum, Shields, Rice and J.

Allum, Rice and myself made the pace at the start and at half-way we were still together. Arthur was setting a fast pace and I knew that my only hope was to keep with him; Bill Rice then fell back and we came across from the Flagstaff, running shoulder to shoulder.

Our boys were placed: Allum 6, Scrimshaw 9, Rice 10, Shields 11—36 points. At the conclusion of three events we have scored 17 out of a possible 18 points and have a 4½ points lead over the next club, Polytechnic Harriers.
